messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Dedicated pool 'polaris-dedicated-us-east-1' node gpu-7c2 experienced 3x NVLINK controller resets; automatic drain initiated for node gpu-7c2. Affected tenant: PolarisFinance (VPC). Triggered 2033456789.

bhargav_oncall: I’m on it. Confirming scope: which tenants on that node?

infra-bot: Allocation map snapshot:
```
node: gpu-7c2
tenants: polarisfinance-prod (3 pods), polarisfinance-analytics (1 pod)
models: llama-70b-quant, redwood/embedding-v2
metrics: token-gen-requests=~27/s
```

sasha_reliability: PolarisFinance prod traffic currently hitting 3 pods that were on gpu-7c2. We should live-migrate or route to fallback. BH, can you cordon and drain fully and trigger routing?

bhargav_oncall: cordoning now.
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7c2 --context=dedicated-us-east-1
kubectl drain gpu-node-7c2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Draining — will route new allocations off.

mara_engineering: I’m taking model routing. Setting routing policy for PolarisFinance to fallback variant 'llama-70b-cpu-quant' for writes, keep embeddings on CPU farm. Applying policy change.

diana_cs: FYI looping in Polaris SRE (external) and Diana from CS will notify them: "We observed GPU node resets; serving degraded for short windows. We're routing to fallback; some requests may see increased latency."

leo_support: Customer impact from logs: 2033456792–2033457030 saw 42 failed generation requests and ~118 latency spikes >2000ms. Error pattern: "kv-cache miss + rate limit retry" in some traces.

bhargav_oncall: Observed AER counters incrementing on PCIe for gpu-7c2; logs show nvlink ECC warnings. Greg, can you confirm hardware vs spot preempt?

greg_hw: Checking host provider logs — this looks like a hardware ECC/regression, not scheduled spot terminate. We have a thermal trip and nvlink reset. Recommending node replace. I'll open a hardware ticket and request replacement farm slot.

infra-bot: Hardware ticket opened: HT-89213 (priority: P1). Expected replacement ETA 4h.

sasha_reliability: For mitigation, keeping routing fallback for PolarisFinance and enabling aggressive KV prefix caching for their common prompts to reduce load on the fallback CPU instances. Also increasing instance concurrency by +20% for embeddings to prevent backlog.

mara_engineering: Applied routing policy change at 2033456840. Canary traffic (10%) stayed on GPU variants for validation, rest moved to CPU-quant. Canary results: generation quality checks passed for 9/10. Latency increased from median 180ms -> 850ms on CPU quant. Acceptable per SLA for short window.

bhargav_oncall: Noting customer-facing statement for Diana:
"Polaris — We detected hardware instability in a GPU node in your dedicated pool. We've routed your traffic to fallback instances; you may see increased latency on some generation requests. We're replacing the affected node; ETA ~4h. We'll post updates to this thread."

diana_cs: Sent to customer at 2033456902. Polaris acknowledged and asked for expected impact on batch jobs. I told them batch analytics will be queued and may take 30–60m extra; they requested a temporary priority bump for scheduled nightly runs.

mara_engineering: Created temporary priority rule for PolarisFinance batch queue (priority: high) to use spare CPU capacity for tonight's window. Applied at 2033456947.

leo_support: Observability: error budget burn increased by 0.7% for Polaris service; we're under threshold but watching.

bhargav_oncall: Handing off to sasha for longer-term coordination and postmortem. I’ll stay reachable for escalation. @sasha_reliability you take?

sasha_reliability: I’m taking the incident. Current actions: 1) node replacement ticket open; 2) routing/fallback in place; 3) customer notified; 4) batch priority applied. Next: run hardware replacement, validate KV cache consistency, run degradation test.

greg_hw: Replacement host allocated; prepping image and driver bundle. ETA to boot-and-join: ~3h45m. I will coordinate with infra ops for safe reboot and NVLink stress test post-provision.

mara_engineering: Two quick follow-ups: 1) we should snapshot the model KV-caches for Polaris before we fully shut down the node (to reduce cold-start cost), 2) add a temporary fallback for embeddings to route to regional embedding cluster eu-west if us-east is overloaded.

bhargav_oncall: Snapshot command queued:
```
/opt/redwood/bin/kv-snapshot --tenant polarisfinance --node gpu-7c2 --out /mnt/snapshots/polaris-2033456789.tar.gz
```
Started at 2033456990, progress 60%.

infra-bot: KV snapshot completed and uploaded to s3://redwood-snapshots/polaris/2033456789.tar.gz

leo_support: A note on telemetry: the fallback saw an initial error spike when we increased concurrency; rolled back one parameter to prevent memory thrash at 2033457008. Stabilized.

sasha_reliability: Running synthetic gen checks now (prompt set: polaris_smoketest_1).

mara_engineering: Results: 95/100 responses returned, 2 degraded (long tail), 3 failed transient. Acceptable for now.

diana_cs: Polaris asked if we can provide a post-incident summary and timeline. I'll capture updates here and send a formal writeup once Sasha posts the postmortem.

greg_hw: Node replacement in progress. PXE boot + driver install started at 2033457050.

bhargav_oncall: Quick note — I toggled canary back to 20% for extra validation while replacement finishes.

mara_engineering: Also added alert rule to monitor NVLINK ECC counters per node to catch similar early resets: rule id infra/alerts/2263.

sasha_reliability: Follow-up checklist for postmortem: - root cause (nvlink ECC + thermal), - why auto-drain triggered but not preempted earlier, - improve early detection rules, - customer comms timeline. Will draft and circulate.

infra-bot: Replacement node gpu-8a1 joined pool at 2033457110. Recovered 3 Polaris pods scheduled onto new node.

greg_hw: Completed NVLink stress test and validated ECC counters stable. Marking hardware ticket HT-89213 -> RESOLVED (swap completed).

sasha_reliability: Validating in prod traffic: error rate down to baseline, latency gradually returning to normal. Leaving routing fallback active for 30m to ensure stability, then revert to normal model routing.

leo_support: Customer confirmed they saw reduced errors at ~2033457115 and appreciate the priority bump for batch window.

sasha_reliability: Reverting fallback at 2033457120 (canary 50% -> 100% back to GPU variants). Monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident update: status=resolved; summary="GPU NVLINK controller resets on node gpu-7c2 in polaris-dedicated-us-east-1; node replaced; routing fallback used; customer notified; postmortem pending." closed_ts=2033457123

sasha_reliability: Posting postmortem draft in #postmortems tomorrow. Thanks everyone for quick coordination.
